text:
arthur: Quick one - onboarding guide shows using an OkHttp Authenticator that does a blocking Retrofit call to refresh tokens. On Android 12+ this sometimes deadlocks under load.

keiko: Do you have a small repro? Sounds like shared client deadlock / dispatcher starvation.

arthur: Minimal repro: spawn 50 concurrent requests with expired token; Authenticator calls authService.refreshSync() which uses the same Retrofit instance. Some calls hang forever and emulator logs show RejectedExecutionException later.

molly: Yep that's the classic pattern we warned about. Two fixes: 1) use a TokenProvider with an async refresh and dedicated client, or 2) use a dedicated OkHttpClient inside Authenticator (but reuse it).

arthur: I tried (2) naively and hit EMFILE after a few hours because I created a new client per refresh. GC didn't close pools fast enough.

keiko: Right — never create a client per request. Reuse a single dedicated client or explicitly shutdown its dispatcher and evict pool if ephemeral. Prefer a singleton.

molly: For onboarding, let's change sampleapp to include the TokenProvider pattern (volatile cached token + single-threaded refresh executor + dedicated client) and add a short blurb in the SDK FAQ.

arthur: Can someone open a tiny PR replacing the Authenticator example? I can add a unit test that simulates high concurrency.

build-bot: Created issue #4451: "sampleapp: replace blocking authenticator pattern with token provider; add concurrency test" - https://git.internal/redwood/issues/4451

keiko: I'll take the PR and update migration notes for v0.13.0. Add a small code comment: "Do not call shared client from Authenticator/Interceptor synchronously."

arthur: Thanks — will send a patch this afternoon. Leaving notes in the onboarding checklist too. :thumbsup:
